From the start, she took the time to do a thorough consultation—asking thoughtful questions about Tella’s needs, our preferences, and even how she could make the grooming process more comfortable for her. That level of care and attention is so rare. 💛

And the result? PERFECTION.
Tella came out looking like she had been waiting her whole life for this haircut! It’s now day 5 and somehow she just keeps getting cuter every single day.

The most unbelievable part—Tella had ZERO stress reactions after the groom. Usually, she gets so anxious that it affects her even the next day, but this time? Nothing. Completely calm, happy, and herself. That alone speaks volumes about Paige’s skill and care.

Also, the shop has the cutest selection of pet accessories! I even found the perfect comb I’ve been searching everywhere for (Labradoodle parents—you know the struggle 😅).

And such a lovely surprise—they sent Tella home with a little goodie bag that had a toy and some treats… which she absolutely LOVES! 🧸🍖 Such a thoughtful touch that made the whole experience even more special.

To top it all off—while walking through Canary Wharf after her groom, Tella got SO many compliments. Multiple pet parents even asked, “Did she just get groomed at Pawsome?!” That says everything!

Safe to say—we’ve found our forever groomer in London. 🐶💖

I am extremely upset with the grooming service my English Cocker Spaniel received. This was our first visit, and despite paying for a professional groom, his back was completely shaved, he was butchered!

English Cocker Spaniels are a recognised double-coated breed, and standard grooming guidance is that the back coat should never be shaved. Shaving a double-coated dog is known to damage the coat structure, causing loss of natural texture, shine, and function. It can also result in irreversible coat damage, where the coat grows back patchy, thicker, or with a different texture or colour. The coat also plays an important role in insulation and temperature regulation especially as its winter now also.

This was not explained or discussed with me in advance, and I would never have consented for them to completely shave my dog. I am extremely upset by the outcome and concerned about the long-term impact on my dog’s coat. The owner even called me a few days later to argue with me and tell me that English cocker spaniels are to be shaved which is not true.

I definitely would not recommend going here.

I brought my dog for grooming, and several issues occurred that should not happen during a professional groom:

• Nails were cut too short, leading to bleeding afterwards
• Paw pads were left completely untrimmed
• Leg hair was noticeably uneven and patchy
• After the groom, my dog kept slipping on the floor because the paw pads had not been trimmed properly, which made walking unsafe and uncomfortable for her

These are technical issues, not behavioural ones.
My dog has been groomed regularly at other salons and has never had these problems.

For her safety and comfort, I had to book another groomer to correct the issues. At the next appointment with another groomer, her paw pads and leg hair were trimmed evenly without any difficulty.

I contacted the salon afterwards and provided photos, but unfortunately the response did not address the concerns about grooming quality.

I hope the team can review and improve their technical standards, as this experience caused unnecessary stress for my dog.

I brought my dog here for grooming, and unfortunately, I was very disappointed with the result. I completely understand that mats can make grooming more difficult, but in this case, the approach seemed rushed and there was no visible effort to try to manage or reduce the mats carefully.

Instead, the only solution offered was to shave him down completely — and even that was done unevenly, leaving patches that look poorly blended. I’ve taken my dog to other groomers in London before, and they have always taken the time to work through mats safely and gently — it just takes longer. Here, it felt like there was a strict time limit, and the goal was simply to finish as quickly as possible.

If your dog has any matting, be aware that they may not attempt to work with it and will likely just clip the coat very short. The only positive was that he smelled nice afterwards. Unfortunately, based on this experience, this was my first and last visit.

I’m sharing this so other dog owners can make an informed choice, especially if their dog needs a bit more patience and care during grooming.
